intro: Searching for the best EIS consultant near you usually means you're raising money for a growing company and want the Enterprise Investment Scheme paperwork handled properly, so investors can claim their reliefs without unpleasant surprises later. You want someone who knows the rules well, works locally or is easy to reach, and can take the compliance burden off your hands. That's exactly the kind of introduction we can help with.
need_heading: What people searching for an EIS consultant usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search are company directors or founders preparing to raise funds under EIS and want expert help with the paperwork and the rules.
needs: You are planning a share issue and want an advance assurance application prepared properly before approaching investors.
You need compliance statements and investor certificates handled correctly once money comes in.
You want reassurance that your proposed use of funds fits the EIS rules before you commit.
You are unsure which of the conditions continue to apply after the investment has been made.
You would rather work with a tax adviser you can speak to locally, or at least reach easily by phone.
context_heading: Choosing the right EIS consultant for you
context: Because you searched for the best, it's worth knowing that no official ranking of EIS consultants exists. "Tax adviser" is not a protected title in the UK, so anyone can use it. Instead, look at qualifications and membership: the Chartered Institute of Taxation confers the CTA qualification and the Association of Taxation Technicians is the other main specialist body, and their members follow Professional Conduct in Relation to Taxation. Many accountants and solicitors also advise on tax.

Tax advisers who charge a fee must be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and HMRC has been tightening standards for paid tax agents. So it is sensible to ask about qualifications, supervision and professional indemnity insurance before you go ahead. On "near me", weigh up whether you want face-to-face meetings locally or whether remote contact suits you better, since EIS work is largely document-based.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your company and what it does, so we can match you with a suitable tax adviser.
Explain the fundraising you have in mind and roughly what stage you are at.
Say whether you have already applied for advance assurance or are starting from scratch.
Mention how you intend to use the funds, as this is central to the EIS rules.
Tell us whether you would prefer a consultant near you or are happy to work remotely.
Include any deadlines or investor conversations already underway, so we can prioritise.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the EIS consultant
questions: What qualifications and professional body memberships do you hold for tax work?
How do you approach an advance assurance application, and what do you need from me?
Which EIS conditions do we need to keep meeting after the investment is made?
How will you handle compliance statements and investor certificates?
Are you supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, and do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
How will you keep us informed as the fundraising progresses?

faqs.q: Do I need advance assurance before raising EIS money?
faqs.a: Advance assurance is not compulsory, but it gives investors more confidence that the shares should qualify for EIS reliefs. An EIS consultant can prepare the application and supporting business plan for you. It is worth discussing timing with your adviser early.

faqs.q: What does an EIS consultant actually do?
faqs.a: They prepare advance assurance applications, compliance statements and investor certificates for growing companies. They also help you check that your use of funds meets the rules. Compliance continues after investment, so their involvement often carries on too.

faqs.q: How can I judge who is best for my company?
faqs.a: There is no official ranking, so look at qualifications, membership of bodies such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, and experience with EIS specifically. Ask about supervision and insurance, and whether they will explain the rules clearly. A short conversation usually tells you a lot.

faqs.q: Can I work with a consultant who isn't local to me?
faqs.a: Yes. Much of the EIS work is document-based, so many companies work with advisers remotely. If you searched for someone near you, it's still worth asking whether phone and email contact would suit you just as well.
